_meta.scope: Russian main army HQ, 24 June - 14 December 1812 (1st Western Army under Barclay; united armies from 3 Aug; Kutuzov from 29 Aug; 'Main Army' formally from 28 Sep). All dates Gregorian (New Style); OS = Julian, 12 days earlier.
_meta.primaryItinerarySource: Day-by-day 'Chronicle of the Patriotic War of 1812' published by the Saratov Museum of Military and Labour Glory (sargmbs.ru, one page per day, New Style dates). It cites: Polikarpov/Nikolsky 'Boevoy kalendar-ezhednevnik' (1913), the ROSSPEN encyclopedia 'Otechestvennaya voyna 1812 goda' (2004), 'Bolshaya Evropeyskaya voyna 1812-1815: Khronika sobytiy' (ROSSPEN 2003), and the 2011 biographical dictionary. Cross-checked where possible against Russian/English Wikipedia, the Brockhaus-Efron (ESBE) article, the Russian Biographical Dictionary (RBS), Kudrinsky 'Vilna v 1812 godu', and N. D. Durnovo's staff diary.
_meta.coordinateSource: ru.wikipedia.org article coordinates (API prop=coordinates) for the modern settlement, rounded to 2 decimals; null where no unambiguous article was found.
_meta.markerCaveat: From 4 Dec Kutuzov's HQ left the Main Army (handed to Tormasov) and travelled with Miloradovich's advance guard and then Chichagov's army; the Main Army itself halted around Olshany/Volozhin and only the Guards went on to Vilna. The itinerary follows the HQ (Kutuzov), as the app's marker does.

itinerary.note: HQ of Barclay's 1st Western Army and Alexander I's Imperial HQ. French cross the Neman at Kovno (12 June OS). Alexander attends Bennigsen's ball at Zakret that evening.
Alexander I and the Imperial HQ leave early morning via Nemenchin for Sventsiany (14 June OS). 1st Army begins its retreat; 3rd and 4th Corps fall back onto Vilna. Barclay stays.

1st Army abandons Vilna in the morning and retreats toward Sventsiany (16 June OS). Last detachment (Shakhovskoy) crosses the Green Bridge at about 8 a.m. and destroys it; stores burned. Napoleon enters about 11:00.

Army concentrating on Sventsiany (5th Corps there 29 June; Alexander already there since 26-27 June). Exact day Barclay's own HQ arrived is not stated in the sources found; by 2 July the army stood on the line Soloki - Sventsiany - Kobylniki.
General retreat to the Drissa camp begins; HQ moves with 2nd and 3rd Corps to Old Daugelishki (Daugeliskis). Rearguards left north of Sventsiany.
2nd, 3rd Corps and 1st Cavalry Corps cross the Disna to Vidzy; Barclay moves HQ there. Murat enters Sventsiany.
HQ at Opsa with 2nd, 3rd Corps and 1st Cavalry Corps; army retreating by night marches, resumed 22:00.
HQ with 2nd and 3rd Corps reaches Belmonty (Akhremovtsy).

itinerary.modernName: near Verkhnedvinsk (camp on the left bank of the Western Dvina opposite the town)
itinerary.note: Leading units enter the Drissa camp (27 June OS - the Poltava anniversary; Alexander's Imperial HQ already at Drissa). Coordinates are of Verkhnedvinsk town, not the camp earthworks.
All corps of the 1st Army are in position in or beside the camp.

After the council of 13 July (1 July OS) the army leaves the camp and crosses to the right bank of the Dvina ('having stood there only three days'). Other sources date the march-off 16 July (4 July OS, ESBE) or 17 July (5 July OS, ru.wikipedia main article) - probably the departure from the Drissa area rather than from the camp.
Army continues up the Dvina in two columns; HQ moves to Priluki.
1st Army reaches Polotsk and camps on the Vitebsk road (6 July OS). Alexander I leaves the army here for Moscow (chronicle: 18 July; en.wikipedia: 19 July).
Main body begins leaving Polotsk for Vitebsk in two columns.
Right column and HQ at Staroye Selo, one march short of Vitebsk.
1st Army reaches Vitebsk, HQ in the town (11 July OS). Ostrovno rearguard actions follow 25-27 July.

Under cover of Pahlen's rearguard fight on the Luchesa, Barclay slips away toward Smolensk during the night of 27/28 July (ESBE: night of 15-16 July OS); Napoleon finds the position empty at dawn on 28 July.
Left and centre columns unite at Porechye, HQ arrives there; Dokhturov's right column reaches Rudnya.
Main body at Moshchinki on the approaches to Smolensk; rearguard still at Porechye.
1st Army bivouacs on the Dnieper under the walls of Smolensk (20 July OS).

Bagration's 2nd Army arrives and camps on the left bank: the two armies are united (22 July OS). Barclay and Bagration had met in person on 2 Aug at Governor Bakhmetev's house; Bagration placed himself under Barclay.

After the council of 6 Aug both armies advance from Smolensk toward Rudnya (Barclay insisting on going no more than three marches). ru.wikipedia dates the advance 27 July OS = 8 Aug. Followed by a week of marches and counter-marches in the Smolensk - Rudnya - Porechye triangle.
Second attempt at the offensive: 1st Army on the Rudnya road about 37 km from Smolensk, just as Napoleon crosses the Dnieper to the south (Krasny, Neverovsky's retreat).
Both armies, turned about on 15 Aug, return to Smolensk as Napoleon arrives before the city (4 Aug OS). 1st Army stays on the right (north) bank; battle 16-18 Aug.

Night of 17/18 Aug Dokhturov evacuates the burning city on Barclay's order (6 Aug OS). The 1st Army then marches off on the night of 18/19 Aug, first north by the Porechye road, then by side roads to the Moscow road. No source found for a 02:00 time.
Battle of Valutino (Lubino): Tuchkov 4th's detachment holds the junction so the 1st Army's columns can reach the Moscow road. Barclay on the field.
Both columns of the 1st Army meet at Solovyovo and cross to the left bank of the Dnieper; Platov's rearguard fights there.
1st Army leaves its camp at Umolye at 21:00 and takes a position at Usvyatye, where Barclay first intended to give battle; Bagration's advance guard in Dorogobuzh.
Position at Usvyatye rejected (Bagration found the left flank weak); 1st Army marches from Andreevka to Dorogobuzh.
1st Army takes position at the town; 2nd Army 5 km south-east.
Both armies pass through Vyazma and fall back north-east to Fyodorovskoye.

Army reaches the position Barclay has chosen for battle. That evening Kutuzov, after a daytime stop in Gzhatsk, arrives and takes command (17 Aug OS). He rejects the position and orders the retreat continued.
Armies leave Tsarevo-Zaimishche, pass through Gzhatsk without halting and stop just east at Ivashkovo, where Miloradovich's reserves from Kaluga join. (Gzhatsk itself: 55.55, 35.00.)
Main forces camp at Durykino after a day's march; rearguard action at Gzhatsk.
Armies fall back from Durykino to the Kolotsky monastery, 8 km west of Borodino; Kutuzov's HQ in the monastery. He sends Toll and Bennigsen to examine the Borodino position.
Army occupies the Borodino position along the Kolocha (22 Aug OS). Shevardino redoubt fight 5 Sep; battle 7 Sep (26 Aug OS).
Kutuzov meant to renew the battle, but on learning the losses gave the order to retreat at midnight (night of 7/8 Sep). Army retires in two columns toward and past Mozhaisk (27 Aug OS).

itinerary.place: Zemlino (HQ at Leutinskoye), east of Mozhaisk
itinerary.note: Main forces at Zemlino; HQ at the village of Leutinskoye. Platov's rearguard gives up Mozhaisk about 09:00 this morning, to Kutuzov's displeasure (Platov replaced by Miloradovich). (Mozhaisk: 55.50, 36.03.)
Army marches 19 km from Zemlino behind the Nara; rearguard action at Krymskoye.
Army falls back 26.5 km; Kutuzov, just promoted field marshal, sets HQ in the manor house.
Army to the Mamonovo area; Kutuzov orders a position fortified for a possible battle (31 Aug OS: 'one march from Moscow').
Army on Bennigsen's position Fili - Vorobyovy Gory; HQ in Fili. Council of war in the peasant Frolov's hut at about 17:00 (1 Sep OS); Kutuzov orders retreat through Moscow onto the Ryazan road.

Army marches through Moscow (Barclay personally directing) and out by the Ryazan road, camping at Panki 16 km beyond (2 Sep OS). Miloradovich negotiates a truce with Murat until 19:00 for the rearguard.
Rest day at Panki on the Ryazan road, waiting for units strung out through Moscow.
Army crosses the Moskva at the Borovsky ferry to the right bank (4 Sep OS); HQ at Kulakovo (ru.wikipedia) / 'in the Bronnitsy area' (chronicle). More than 40,000 civilian carts cross with it.
The flank march begins: main forces turn sharply west off the Ryazan road and march along the south bank of the Pakhra toward Podolsk, Raevsky's rearguard holding the heights at the ferry (5 Sep OS).
Army marches 15 km west and camps at Podolsk (6 Sep OS); rests there 19 Sep.
Army reaches the Old Kaluga road (Gorki); Kutuzov's HQ already at Krasnaya Pakhra, where Chernyshev arrives from the Tsar. Main forces cross the Pakhra and camp there 21 Sep (9 Sep OS).

After a week at Krasnaya Pakhra the army falls back down the Old Kaluga road (ru.wikipedia: to Babenki on 14 Sep OS = 26 Sep; chronicle: decision to go to Tarutino 26 Sep, main forces in the Voronovo area by 28 Sep).
Main forces around Voronovo, HQ in the village of Mocha. Same day the 1st and 2nd Western Armies are merged into the 'Main Army'.
Main forces fall back from Voronovo to Spas-Kuplya and rest there 2 Oct; rearguard actions at Spas-Kuplya/Chernishnya 3-4 Oct.

Army marches about 14 km and halts behind Tarutino on the Nara; fortified camp begun; flank march ends (21 Sep OS). HQ had reached Tarutino on 2 Oct (20 Sep OS, ru.wikipedia). ESBE dates the camp from 22 Sep OS (4 Oct). Barclay leaves the army; Kutuzov takes direct command.
HQ moved from Tarutino village to Letashevka on the Old Kaluga road, a few km behind the camp; it stays there until 23 Oct. Lauriston received on the night of 5 Oct.
Battle of Tarutino (Vinkovo), 6 Oct OS: attack on Murat on the Chernishnya 8 km north of the camp begins about 07:00; troops back in camp by 16:00. Kutuzov stays with the Guard in reserve.

Overnight 22/23 Oct Kutuzov receives Dokhturov's report (from Seslavin's sighting at Fominskoye) that Napoleon is marching on Maloyaroslavets; the Main Army breaks camp and marches via Verkhniye Kolodezi, Zhelezny Zavod and Peredol. ESBE: main forces left on the evening of 11 Oct OS.
Main body arrives about 16:00 during the battle (12 Oct OS); Borozdin's 8th Corps relieves Dokhturov. 25 Oct: both armies stand facing each other; Kutuzov pulls back about 2.5 versts south.

Fearing a turning move via Medyn, Kutuzov withdraws the main forces south to Detchino in the night of 25/26 Oct, leaving Miloradovich at Maloyaroslavets (14 Oct OS). Same day Napoleon turns north for the Smolensk road.
HQ in the Goncharov estate 15-17 Oct OS (27-29 Oct); main forces between Polotnyany Zavod and Detchino 27-28 Oct.

Once it is clear the French have left Maloyaroslavets and Borovsk, the Main Army moves from Polotnyany Zavod to Adamovskoye (north of Medyn). The army marched through the Medyn area but no source found puts the HQ in Medyn town (54.97, 35.87).
Main Army from Adamovskoye to Kremenskoye. 31 Oct it starts north toward Vereya and only in the evening is turned sharply west.
Army reaches Silenki (Durnovo's diary: HQ to 'Selenki, on the great Gzhatsk road', 20 Oct OS) and goes on toward Dubrovo.
Kutuzov moves from Silenki to Dubrovo, about 29 km from Vyazma (21 Oct OS, Durnovo). He hands day-to-day command of the Main Army's corps to Tormasov.

While Miloradovich and Platov fight the battle of Vyazma, the main forces only march from Dubrovo to Bykovo, about 10 km south of the town (22 Oct OS); HQ at Bykovo. Only Uvarov's cuirassiers are sent forward.
Army turns sharply south-west from Bykovo toward Yelnya; HQ at the village of Krasnoye (not Krasny). 6 Nov: HQ at Gavryukovo. 7 Nov: HQ at Bely Kholm.
Main Army arrives at Yelnya (27 Oct OS = 8 Nov; one local source converts it to 9 Nov) and rests there 9 Nov.
HQ moves from Yelnya to Baltutino (chronicle spells it 'Bolturino'; Durnovo: Baltutino) on the Roslavl road.
HQ to Lobkovo (Labkovo) on the Roslavl - Smolensk road (30 Oct OS, Durnovo); remains 12 Nov. Troops advance slowly 'sparing their strength'.
Main Army begins the move on Krasny; HQ reaches Shchelkanovo (1 Nov OS, Durnovo).
Main forces (four infantry corps, two cuirassier divisions) halt at Yurovo, 29 km from Krasny, and stay there 15 Nov while Miloradovich cuts the road.
Main forces and HQ at Shilovo, about 5 km (7 versts, Durnovo) from Krasny, 4 Nov OS; detachments occupy Novosyolki and Uvarovo. HQ still here during the fighting of 17 Nov (5 Nov OS).

Army occupies Krasny; HQ at Dobroye just west of the town (6 Nov OS, Durnovo: '2 versts from Krasny'); remains 19 Nov. Ney's corps destroyed on the 18th by Miloradovich. Identification with modern Bolshaya Dobraya is probable, not certain. (Krasny: 54.56, 31.44.)

Army leaves Krasny for Kopys, marching south of and parallel to the Orsha road. Chronicle puts HQ at Laninka/Lanniki 20-21 Nov; a Kutuzov letter of 8 Nov OS (20 Nov) is headed 'Main HQ, Romanovo'. 22 Nov: rest day (trains behind). Coordinates are for Lenino, the modern name of Romanovo.
Army approaches the Dnieper; HQ at Morozovo; Miloradovich sent ahead to Kopys to prepare the crossing.

Army marches along the Dnieper from Morozovo to Kopys; HQ there (12 Nov OS). 25 Nov (13 Nov OS): thanksgiving service, then the troops begin crossing the Dnieper; a Kutuzov dispatch to Chichagov is dated 'Kopys, 13 November'.

Army completes the Dnieper crossing, leaving 144 guns at Kopys as surplus 'because of the great loss of men'; HQ at Staroselye. (One LiveJournal chronology has Kutuzov leaving Kopys 26 Nov, consistent.)

HQ to Krugloye. 28 Nov: army to the Ukhvaly area, HQ at Somry. 29 Nov: HQ at Mikheevichi (Miloradovich's advance guard occupies Borisov). 30 Nov: HQ at Shevernichi. The Berezina battle (26-29 Nov) is fought without the Main Army.

The Main Army crosses the Berezina at Zhukovets, well south of Borisov, two days after Napoleon burned the Studyanka bridges (19 Nov OS); HQ at the village of Usha. ru.wikipedia has the army setting out from Mikheevichi for Zhukovets on 29 Nov.
Army marches south-west from the Berezina; HQ at Rovanichi (Ravanichi). 3 Dec: rest day.

Kutuzov leaves the Main Army (which goes to Shipyany under Tormasov) and moves his HQ by post-horses to Kosino, where Miloradovich's advance guard stands, in order to join Chichagov's army. 5 Dec: HQ at Beloruchi. Identification of Kosino with the Logoisk-district village is probable.

HQ arrives at Radoshkovichi with Miloradovich's troops and is still there 7 Dec; Kutuzov's report to the Tsar of 25 Nov OS (7 Dec) is dated from 'Main HQ, Radashkevichi'. The Main Army rests at (Ostroshitsky) Gorodok.
HQ with the advance guard at Molodechno. 9 Dec: Miloradovich occupies Smorgon.

Kutuzov and HQ reach Oshmyany. Russian troops (Chichagov's advance guard, Cossacks) occupy Vilna the same day (28 Nov OS). The Main Army is ordered to halt at Olshany, only the Guards and grenadiers to go on to Vilna.

Kutuzov arrives in Vilna: 30 Nov OS = 12 Dec per Kudrinsky; 29 Nov OS = 11 Dec ('left Oshmyany in the morning, reached Vilna by the end of the day') per the sargmbs chronicle, 1812w.ru and vgd.ru. Chichagov meets him with a report and the city keys; that evening the theatre shows his portrait inscribed 'To the saviour of the fatherland'. HQ remains here to the end of the year.

OUTSIDE THE 24 JUN-14 DEC WINDOW, for reference: Alexander I arrives by sledge about 7 p.m. on 11 Dec OS (23 Dec), having left St Petersburg 7 (19) Dec; Kutuzov meets him at the palace steps and receives the Order of St George 1st class. Vigel gives 12 Dec OS; a LiveJournal chronology gives 22 Dec NS.

moments.title: The ball at Zakret
moments.body: While the Grande Armee crossed the Neman at Kovno, Alexander I was at a ball given by Bennigsen and the staff adjutants at Bennigsen's country house of Zakret outside Vilna. In Kudrinsky's account (from de Sanglen) the Tsar was told of the Kovno dispatch before the ball and said he had expected it, but the ball would go ahead; the popular version has Balashov whispering the news during the dancing.

quote.text: Я этого ожидал... но бал все таки будет
quote.author: Alexander I (as reported by de Sanglen)

moments.title: Balashov sent to Napoleon
moments.body: Alexander issued his order to the armies announcing war and sent his police minister, Adjutant-General Balashov, to Napoleon offering talks if the French withdrew behind the Neman. Balashov was held at the outposts, carried back to Vilna and received by Napoleon there on 1 July - in the city he had left five days earlier. Nothing came of it.

quote.text: Я с вами. На начинающего бог.
quote.author: Alexander I

moments.title: Vilna given up without battle
moments.body: Barclay kept two corps in front of Vilna until his flank corps were clear, then marched for Sventsiany on the morning of 28 June. The stores were burned, and at about eight the last detachment crossed the Green Bridge over the Viliya and destroyed it. Napoleon rode in around eleven.

moments.title: Drissa judged a trap
moments.body: Four days after the army filed into Pfuel's fortified camp on the Dvina, Alexander held a council there with Barclay, Volkonsky, Arakcheev, Michaud and others. The camp was condemned - Clausewitz, who had inspected it, thought an army staying there would be taken in rear and pinned in its own half-circle of trenches - and the army marched out next day for Polotsk and Vitebsk to reach Bagration.

moments.title: The Tsar leaves the army
moments.body: At Polotsk, persuaded by Shishkov, Arakcheev and Balashov that he was needed to raise reserves and rally the country, Alexander left the army for Moscow. Before going he signed the appeal to Moscow and the manifesto calling out a militia. Barclay was left in command of the 1st Army but with no authority over Bagration.

moments.title: Slipping away from Vitebsk
moments.body: Barclay had drawn up at Vitebsk hoping Bagration would join him through Orsha; learning that Davout had blocked Bagration at Mogilev, he left Pahlen's rearguard fighting on the Luchesa and marched off for Smolensk in the night. Napoleon, who had postponed his attack expecting a battle, found the camp empty at dawn.

moments.title: The two armies unite
moments.body: Bagration's 2nd Army marched into Smolensk and camped on the left bank of the Dnieper, ending a 35-day, 750-kilometre retreat. Napoleon had failed to beat the Russian armies separately. The day before, Bagration, though senior in rank, had placed himself under Barclay.

moments.title: The abortive Rudnya offensive
moments.body: Pressed by Bagration and most of the generals, Barclay agreed on 6 August to attack toward Rudnya - on condition the army went no further than three marches from Smolensk. A week of hesitant marches and counter-marches between Smolensk, Rudnya and Porechye followed, and while it lasted Napoleon crossed the Dnieper and came at Smolensk from the south. The quarrel between the two commanders became open.

moments.title: Smolensk abandoned, burning
moments.body: After two days' fighting for the walls Barclay ordered Dokhturov out of the blazing city in the night; many inhabitants left with the troops. Russian Wikipedia puts the army leaving at 76,000 under Barclay with Bagration's 34,000 covering the Dorogobuzh road. The generals' anger at another retreat finished Barclay's standing with the army.

moments.title: Kutuzov takes command
moments.body: A special committee in St Petersburg unanimously chose Kutuzov on 17 August and Alexander confirmed him on the 20th. He reached the army at Tsarevo-Zaimishche on the evening of 29 August after a stop in Gzhatsk, looked at the position Barclay had picked for a battle, rejected it, and ordered the retreat to go on toward his reinforcements.

moments.title: The choice of Borodino
moments.body: From the Kolotsky monastery Kutuzov sent Toll and Bennigsen ahead to examine the ground; on 3 September the army filed onto a position along the Kolocha by the village of Borodino, its right near Maslovo and its left at Shevardino. Miloradovich had just brought in reserves from Kaluga, and Moscow militia were arriving.

moments.title: The order to retreat
moments.body: On the evening of Borodino Kutuzov reported the battle to the Tsar as a victory and meant to fight again in the morning. Then the loss returns came in, and at midnight he ordered the army back through Mozhaisk. Russian losses are put at 40-45 thousand killed and wounded.

moments.title: The council at Fili
moments.body: In the peasant Frolov's hut at Fili the generals argued whether to fight on Bennigsen's position before Moscow. Bennigsen, Yermolov, Konovnitsyn, Uvarov and Dokhturov were for a battle; Barclay, Osterman-Tolstoy, Raevsky and Toll for retreat. Kutuzov sided with the minority and ordered the army through Moscow onto the Ryazan road. No minutes were kept.

quote.text: с потерей Москвы не потеряна ещё Россия
quote.author: M. I. Kutuzov
quote.work: at the council at Fili, as given in ru.wikipedia 'Совет в Филях'

moments.title: Through Moscow
moments.body: The army marched through the city and out by the Ryazan road, most of the inhabitants leaving with it. Governor Rostopchin, taken by surprise by the decision, sent away the fire engines, ordered the police to destroy what they could by fire, and left for Vladimir. Miloradovich, with the rearguard, got Murat to agree a truce until seven in the evening by threatening to fight in the streets.

moments.title: The flank march fools Murat
moments.body: Having crossed the Moskva at the Borovsky ferry, the army turned sharply west along the Pakhra toward Podolsk and the Old Kaluga road. Cossack regiments left on the Ryazan, Kashira and Tula roads were told to retire along those roads, and Efremov's Cossacks drew Murat's cavalry two marches toward Bronnitsy. Sebastiani realised he had lost the army only on the night of 21-22 September.

moments.title: Not one step further back
moments.body: The army halted behind the Nara at Tarutino and began entrenching; Kutuzov's headquarters settled at Letashevka. For nearly three weeks it rested, drew recruits and remounts, and waited. Brockhaus-Efron says it grew to 97,000 men not counting Cossacks and militia; 26 regiments of Don Cossack militia rode in.

quote.author: M. I. Kutuzov
quote.work: as reported by Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky (via ru.wikipedia 'Тарутинский манёвр')

moments.title: Lauriston comes for peace
moments.body: Napoleon's envoy General Lauriston was brought to Kutuzov at Tarutino late in the evening. Kutuzov's agreeing to see him at all alarmed Wilson and Bennigsen, since the Tsar had forbidden any talks while an armed Frenchman stood on Russian soil. Kutuzov told Lauriston he had no authority to treat.

moments.title: The small war
moments.body: From Letashevka Kutuzov organised the flying detachments west of Moscow - Dorokhov's, the largest, sent to take Vereya - while Davydov, Figner and Seslavin raided the Smolensk road. Partisan leaders were told to hand captured muskets to the peasants and use them to escort prisoners to the Tarutino camp.

moments.title: Tarutino: the first attack
moments.body: A night march meant to surround Murat's advance guard on the Chernishnya went astray; only Orlov-Denisov's Cossacks were in place at dawn and attacked alone at seven. Murat lost up to 4,000 men and 38 guns; the Russians about 1,500, General Baggovut among the dead. Kutuzov stayed with the Guard and would not push further.

moments.title: Seslavin sees the Grande Armee
moments.body: Around eight in the evening Captain Seslavin's partisans, watching the New Kaluga road near Fominskoye, found Napoleon's main army on the march; a captured Guardsman said Moscow had been abandoned and the army was bound for Maloyaroslavets. Dokhturov, who had been about to attack what he took for a detachment, sent the news on to Kutuzov.

moments.title: Kutuzov weeps: Moscow is free
moments.body: Dokhturov's staff officer Major Bolgovskoy reached Letashevka in the night with the report that Napoleon had left Moscow. By the account that Tolstoy later worked into War and Peace, the old field marshal turned to the icons, crossed himself and wept. The army was ordered out of camp for Maloyaroslavets at once.

moments.title: Maloyaroslavets
moments.body: Dokhturov attacked at five in the morning; the town changed hands eight times (some accounts say more) and ended in French possession. Kutuzov's main body came up about four in the afternoon and stood across the Kaluga road behind it. Each side lost about 7,000. Two nights later Kutuzov fell back south to Detchino and Polotnyany Zavod - and Napoleon, the same day, turned north for the ruined Smolensk road.

moments.title: Parallel pursuit, not a blow
moments.body: While Miloradovich and Platov, with 25-30 thousand men, cut into Davout's corps at Vyazma, Kutuzov's main body merely marched from Dubrovo to Bykovo, ten kilometres south of the town, and sent forward only cuirassiers. Staff officers who wanted the road blocked were refused: he would not, one recalled, risk a tired army 'on a venture'.

moments.title: Krasny: the golden bridge
moments.body: With the main army at Shilovo, five kilometres from Krasny, Kutuzov cancelled a night attack on learning Napoleon was still in the town, and held Tormasov's enveloping column back until two in the afternoon. The Guard got away to Orsha; Davout's and then Ney's corps were wrecked behind it. The British commissioner Wilson accused him of letting Napoleon go on purpose.

quote.text: I prefer giving my enemy a 'pont d'or', as you call it, to receiving a 'coup de collier'
quote.author: M. I. Kutuzov, as recorded by Sir Robert Wilson
quote.work: Wilson, Narrative of Events during the Invasion of Russia (via en.wikipedia 'Battle of Krasnoi')

moments.title: The pursuers are dying too
moments.body: Crossing the Dnieper at Kopys, the Main Army left 144 guns behind as surplus 'because of the great loss of men'. About 100,000 had marched from Tarutino; within three weeks no more than half were in the ranks, though battle had cost only some 10,000 - the rest had fallen out on forced marches over snow-covered roads.

quote.text: Всё это развалится и без меня
quote.author: M. I. Kutuzov
quote.work: quoted by N. P. Mikhnevich (via ru.wikipedia 'Сражение под Красным')

moments.title: Late to the Berezina
moments.body: When Napoleon forced the Berezina at Studyanka on 26-29 November, Kutuzov's headquarters was still between Kopys and Krugloye, several marches away; Chichagov and Wittgenstein fought without him. The Main Army crossed at Zhukovets, far downstream, on 1 December, two days after the French burned their bridges.

moments.title: Kutuzov rides ahead
moments.body: Leaving the worn-out Main Army to Tormasov, Kutuzov went forward by relays of post-horses - ten carts and sixty horses waiting at each station - to join Miloradovich's advance guard and Chichagov's fresher army. The Main Army was soon halted to rest around Olshany; only the Guards went on to Vilna.

moments.title: Back in Vilna
moments.body: Kutuzov, twice governor of the city, re-entered Vilna two days after the first Russian troops. Chichagov met him with a report and the keys; the theatre showed his portrait inscribed 'To the saviour of the fatherland'; he slept in rooms that had been heated for Napoleon. Of 97,112 men who left Tarutino, Kudrinsky counts 27,464 reaching Vilna. The streets and hospitals were choked with French dead.

moments.title: The Tsar returns
moments.body: (After the 14 December cut-off.) Alexander drove into Vilna by sledge at about seven in the evening, six months after the ball at Zakret. Kutuzov met him at the palace steps with the parade state and was given the Order of St George, first class, though the Tsar's dissatisfaction with the pursuit was no secret. Next day, his birthday, Alexander told the generals they had saved not Russia alone but Europe.

quote.text: Вы спасли не одну Россию, вы спасли Европу!
quote.author: Alexander I
quote.work: to his generals at Vilna, 12 (24) December 1812 (Kudrinsky, Vilna v 1812 godu)

strength.scope: 1st Western Army (Barclay) at the opening of the campaign
strength.source: Brockhaus-Efron Encyclopedic Dictionary (ESBE), 'Отечественная война 1812 года': '1-я армия (120 т.)'

strength.scope: 1st Western Army, upper end of the range '120-136 thousand' given in the ru.wikipedia table for 24 June 1812 (two cited sources; lower end 120,000)
strength.source: ru.wikipedia 'Отечественная война 1812 года', table of forces, notes 93-94

strength.scope: 1st AND 2nd Western Armies together at the start, with 758 guns (for comparison with the united army at Smolensk)
strength.source: ru.wikipedia 'Отечественная война 1812 года', note 64

strength.scope: Total Russian force at Smolensk, both armies (30,000 engaged)
strength.source: Bodart 1908, p. 436, as cited in en.wikipedia 'Battle of Smolensk (1812)'

strength.scope: Barclay withdraws with 76,000; Bagration's 34,000 cover the Dorogobuzh road (76,000 + 34,000)
strength.source: ru.wikipedia 'Отечественная война 1812 года'

strength.scope: Regulars only, both armies (1st Army 75,373 with 420 guns); excludes Cossacks and militia
strength.source: Army returns as given on napoleon-series.org, 'Russian Artillery on the Eve of the Battle of Borodino' (figure from search-result extract; page not opened in full)

strength.scope: Toll's memoirs: 95,000 regulars + 7,000 Cossacks + 10,000 militia; 640 guns
strength.source: K. F. Toll, as tabulated in ru.wikipedia 'Бородинское сражение'

strength.scope: Bogdanovich: 103,000 regulars + 7,000 Cossacks + 10,000 militia; 640 guns (his table total is given as 120,800)
strength.source: M. I. Bogdanovich, as tabulated in ru.wikipedia 'Бородинское сражение'

strength.scope: Troitsky: 115,302 regulars + 11,000 Cossacks + 28,500 militia; 640 guns. (ru.wikipedia infobox: 'more than 154 thousand incl. about 9,500 Cossacks and over 31,000 militia, 624 guns'; about 31,000 militia had no firearms.)
strength.source: N. A. Troitsky, as tabulated in ru.wikipedia 'Бородинское сражение'

strength.scope: Clausewitz's total for the Russian army at Borodino (he served with it)
strength.source: Clausewitz, as tabulated in ru.wikipedia 'Бородинское сражение' (historians' table also: Buturlin 132,000; Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky 128,000; Tarle 127,800; Beskrovny 126,000; Vasiliev 155,200; Zemtsov 154,000; Bezotosny 150,000)

strength.scope: Regular army after the battle, 'most probable' figure; excludes Cossacks, militia and the reinforcements that arrived afterwards. UNVERIFIED AT SOURCE: taken from a search-result summary; the PDF could not be opened.
strength.source: S. V. Shvedov, 'Численность и потери русской армии в Бородинском сражении' (Borodino conference, 1994)

strength.scope: Low end of ru.wikipedia's 'from 85,000 to 120,000' growth during the camp, incl. militia (alternative range from I. Isaev, Voenno-istorichesky zhurnal 1962 no. 10: 60,000 on arrival to 130,000)
strength.source: ru.wikipedia 'Тарутинский лагерь'

strength.scope: Isaev's lower figure for the army on arrival at Tarutino (rising to 130,000 by departure)
strength.source: I. Isaev, Voenno-istorichesky zhurnal, 1962, no. 10, pp. 111-113, as cited in ru.wikipedia 'Тарутинский лагерь'

strength.scope: Main Army 'strengthened to 97,000 men, not counting Cossacks and militia' during the stay at Tarutino; elsewhere in the same article '100 thousand men with 622 guns'
strength.source: Brockhaus-Efron (ESBE), 'Отечественная война 1812 года'

strength.scope: Total Russian strength at Tarutino (36,000 committed to the attack on Murat - Bodart)
strength.source: Sir Robert Wilson 1860, p. 208, as cited in the infobox of en.wikipedia 'Battle of Tarutino'

strength.scope: 97,000 regular troops PLUS 20,000 Cossacks and more than 10,000 militia (ratniki), 622 guns - i.e. about 127,000 all told
strength.source: ru.wikipedia 'Отечественная война 1812 года' (footnoted)

strength.scope: Men who marched out of Tarutino (the starting figure for the famous comparison with Vilna)
strength.source: S. Kudrinsky, 'Вильна в 1812 году'

strength.scope: Russian army assembled at the town by evening ('up to 90 thousand', about 31,800 actually engaged); ru.wikipedia: 'more than 90,000 soldiers and 600 guns'
strength.source: sargmbs.ru chronicle, 24 October; ru.wikipedia 'Сражение под Малоярославцем'

strength.scope: NOT the whole army: Miloradovich's advance guard plus Platov's Cossack corps, '25 to 30 thousand' in the ranks; the main body did not fight
strength.source: sargmbs.ru chronicle, 3 November

strength.scope: '50 to 60 thousand regular troops', plus about 20,000 Cossacks and nearly 500 guns
strength.source: Russian Ministry of Defence page as cited in ru.wikipedia 'Сражение под Красным' (same range in en.wikipedia 'Battle of Krasnoi')

strength.scope: Men Kutuzov 'had at hand' on the evening of 17 November (ru.wikipedia infobox: 60-80 thousand)
strength.source: ru.wikipedia 'Сражение под Красным'

strength.scope: Kutuzov's main body approaching Krasny from the south on 16 November (excluding Miloradovich's 18,000 and Ozharovsky's 3,500)
strength.source: en.wikipedia 'Battle of Krasnoi' (citing Chandler et al.)

strength.scope: 'About 100 thousand left Tarutino; within three weeks no more than half remained', combat losses only about 10,000 - Mikhnevich. Upper bound, not a count.
strength.source: N. P. Mikhnevich (2003 ed.), as cited in ru.wikipedia 'Сражение под Красным'

strength.scope: Zamoyski, following Buturlin: Kutuzov lost 30,000 men between Maloyaroslavets and Krasny and as many again fell behind, leaving 26,500 available (as summarised from en.wikipedia; wording not checked against Zamoyski)
strength.source: A. Zamoyski / D. Buturlin, as cited in en.wikipedia 'Battle of Krasnoi'

strength.scope: Men of the Main Army who reached Vilna, of 97,112 who left Tarutino
strength.source: S. Kudrinsky, 'Вильна в 1812 году'

strength.scope: Main Army at Vilna, with 200 guns (down from 100,000 with 622 guns at Tarutino) - probably counting non-combatants / all arms where the 27,464 figure counts men in the ranks
strength.source: Brockhaus-Efron (ESBE), 'Отечественная война 1812 года'

strength.scope: 'Russian field army reduced to 40,000 effectives by the time they reached the Neman' (lead of en.wikipedia; citation there is Mikaberidze 2020, pp. 556-557, attribution to this exact figure not verified)
strength.source: en.wikipedia 'French invasion of Russia'

strength.scope: Bogdanovich's figure for the 'main army' at the capture of Vilna as reported by en.wikipedia (down from about 150,000 at the start; total shortfall 210,000, of whom up to 40,000 returned to the ranks) - almost certainly a wider definition than Kutuzov's own Main Army
strength.source: M. I. Bogdanovich, as cited in en.wikipedia 'French invasion of Russia'

strength.scope: 'No more than 12,000 men remained in the Main Army' in mid-December (alongside 17-18,000 with Chichagov and 34-36,000 with Wittgenstein) - lowest figure found; basis unclear
strength.source: Russian Biographical Dictionary (RBS), vol. 9 (1903), article on Kutuzov, p. 649

corrections: STRENGTH CURVE, END: '100,000 from 18 Oct flat to the end' is wrong. Sourced points: 97,112 marched out of Tarutino (Kudrinsky) / 97,000 regulars + 20,000 Cossacks + 10,000+ militia on 22 Oct (ru.wikipedia); about 90,000 at Maloyaroslavets 24 Oct; 50-60,000 regulars at Krasny 16-18 Nov (already 'no more than half' of the Tarutino strength, Mikhnevich); 144 guns abandoned at Kopys 26 Nov for want of men; 27,464 in the ranks at Vilna (Kudrinsky) or 42,000 with 200 guns (ESBE). The marker's force lost roughly 55-70% between 23 Oct and 12 Dec, overwhelmingly to march attrition, cold and sickness, not battle.

STRENGTH CURVE, BORODINO: '125,000 on 7 Sep' sits inside the range but hides the definitional split - 113,000 regulars (returns) / 112,000 (Toll) / 120,000 (Bogdanovich, Clausewitz) versus about 155,000 counting all Cossacks and militia (Troitsky, Vasiliev). '90,000 on 9 Sep' is too high for regulars: Russian losses were 40-45,000 and Shvedov's estimate for the regular army after the battle is about 64,000 (unverified at source). 90,000 is only defensible if militia and Cossacks are included; label whichever is used.

PURSUIT ROUTE: the HQ was never at Medyn (30 Oct). Sourced sequence: Maloyaroslavets 24-25 Oct -> Detchino 26 Oct -> Polotnyany Zavod 27-29 Oct -> Adamovskoye 29 Oct -> Kremenskoye 30 Oct -> (feint north toward Vereya 31 Oct) -> Silenki 1 Nov -> Dubrovo 2 Nov -> Bykovo 3 Nov -> Krasnoye 5 Nov -> Gavryukovo 6 Nov -> Bely Kholm 7 Nov -> Yelnya 8-9 Nov -> Baltutino 10 Nov -> Lobkovo 11-12 Nov -> Shchelkanovo 13 Nov -> Yurovo 14-15 Nov -> Shilovo 16-17 Nov -> Dobroye 18-19 Nov -> Romanovo/Lanniki 20-22 Nov -> Morozovo 23 Nov -> Kopys 24-25 Nov -> Staroselye 26 Nov -> Krugloye 27 Nov -> Somry 28 Nov -> Mikheevichi 29 Nov -> Shevernichi 30 Nov -> Zhukovets (Berezina)/Usha 1 Dec -> Rovanichi 2-3 Dec.

KRASNY: 'Krasny 16-19 Nov' misplaces the HQ. It was at Shilovo, about 5 km short of the town, on 16-17 Nov (the days of the main fighting) and moved to Dobroye beside Krasny only on 18 Nov, staying 19 Nov; it left for Kopys on 20 Nov.

AFTER THE BEREZINA: on 4 Dec Kutuzov left the Main Army (handed to Tormasov, halted to rest around Olshany/Volozhin) and rode ahead with a small HQ: Kosino 4 Dec, Beloruchi 5 Dec, Radoshkovichi 6-7 Dec (not just 7 Dec), Molodechno 8 Dec, Oshmyany 10 Dec, Vilna 11 or 12 Dec. So from 4 Dec the marker is a headquarters, not ~30,000 men - only the Guards followed it into Vilna. The strength shown with the marker should say so.
KOPYS: HQ arrived 24 Nov (not 25 Nov); 25 Nov was the thanksgiving service and start of the Dnieper crossing; HQ left for Staroselye 26 Nov.

SVENTSIANY: 'Sventsiany 2 Jul' is the wrong way round - the army fell back on Sventsiany on 28-29 June (Alexander had gone there on 26 June) and LEFT on 3 July for Vidzy (4 Jul), Opsa (6 Jul), Belmonty (7 Jul).

DRISSA: 'Drissa camp 11-16 Jul' should be arrive 9 Jul (lead units; all in by 11 Jul), council 13 Jul, camp abandoned 14 Jul (army crossed to the right bank). 16 Jul (4 July OS, ESBE) / 17 Jul (5 July OS, ru.wikipedia) are given for the march-off toward Polotsk; by 16 Jul the HQ was already at Priluki.

VILNA ABANDONED '28 Jun 04:00': no source for 04:00. The army left on the morning of 28 June (16 June OS); the last detachment crossed and destroyed the Green Bridge at about 08:00; Napoleon entered about 11:00.
PORECHYE: HQ reached Porechye on 29 Jul, not 31 Jul (on 31 Jul the main body was at Moshchinki; on 1 Aug under the walls of Smolensk).

SMOLENSK: the 1st Army was at Smolensk from 1 Aug; the union is dated 3 Aug (22 July OS) because that is when Bagration's army arrived. 'Leaves Smolensk 18 Aug 02:00' - no source for the hour: the city was evacuated in the night of 17/18 Aug, and the 1st Army marched away from the north bank on the night of 18/19 Aug. The Solovyovo crossing was 20 Aug.
GZHATSK '1 Sep': the armies passed through Gzhatsk on 31 Aug without halting (camp at Ivashkovo just east); 1 Sep was Durykino; 2 Sep the Kolotsky monastery; 3 Sep Borodino (correct).
BORODINO WITHDRAWAL '8 Sep 02:00': the sourced detail is that Kutuzov gave the order to retreat at midnight (night of 7/8 Sep). No source for 02:00.

MOZHAISK '9 Sep': the main army passed Mozhaisk on 8 Sep; on 9 Sep it was at Zemlino (HQ Leutinskoye) and the rearguard lost Mozhaisk that morning. Then Krutitsy 10 Sep, Bolshiye Vyazyomy 11 Sep, Mamonovo 12 Sep, Fili 13 Sep.
FILI COUNCIL '16:00': sources give about 17:00 (5 p.m.) on 13 Sep (1 Sep OS).

FLANK MARCH: Borovsky ferry crossing was 16 Sep (4 Sep OS), not 17 Sep - 17 Sep is the turn west; Podolsk was reached 18 Sep (6 Sep OS), not 19 Sep (a rest day there); Krasnaya Pakhra 20-21 Sep (9 Sep OS) is right. Missing halts: Panki 14-15 Sep; Voronovo/Mocha 28 Sep; Spas-Kuplya 1-2 Oct.
TARUTINO: arrival 3 Oct and departure 23 Oct are right, but the HQ itself sat at Letashevka (about 5 km south-west on the Old Kaluga road) from 6 Oct, not in Tarutino village.

KUTUZOV'S APPOINTMENT: committee vote 17 Aug (5 Aug OS), imperial confirmation 20 Aug (8 Aug OS), arrival with the army 29 Aug evening at Tsarevo-Zaimishche (17 Aug OS). On 29 Aug the French entered Vyazma, so 'Vyazma 27 Aug' for the Russians (arrive) is right but they left it on the 28th.
ALEXANDER'S ARRIVAL IN VILNA is 23 Dec (11 Dec OS), outside a 24 Jun-14 Dec window; do not show it as part of the campaign's last day.
openQuestions: Kutuzov's arrival in Vilna: 12 Dec (30 Nov OS) per Kudrinsky 'Vilna v 1812 godu' and a LiveJournal chronology; 11 Dec (29 Nov OS) per the sargmbs chronicle (left Oshmyany in the morning, arrived by evening), 1812w.ru and vgd.ru. Both are plausible (late-evening arrival on the 11th, public reception on the 12th). The app's '12 Dec' is defensible; note the alternative.
Alexander I's arrival in Vilna: 23 Dec (11 Dec OS), about 19:00, per Kudrinsky and the Russian Biographical Dictionary; Vigel gives 12 Dec OS (24 Dec); one LiveJournal chronology gives 22 Dec NS.
Date Alexander left the army at Polotsk: 18 Jul (sargmbs chronicle) vs 19 Jul (en.wikipedia); probably the night of 18/19 July (6-7 July OS).

Departure from the Drissa camp: 14 Jul (chronicle: crossed the Dvina after three days in camp) vs 16 Jul (ESBE: 'marched for Vitebsk on 4 July' OS) vs 17 Jul (ru.wikipedia: '5 (17) July'). ru.wikipedia 'Дрисский лагерь' has Alexander arriving at Drissa on 1 (13) July, whereas the chronicle has his Imperial HQ already there on 9 July.
Start of the Rudnya offensive: 7 Aug (chronicle, en.wikipedia) vs 8 Aug (27 July OS, ru.wikipedia). HQ locations during 7-15 Aug were not found; rows for those days carry no HQ village.
Exactly when Barclay's own HQ reached Sventsiany (27-29 June) was not found; the Imperial HQ went there 26 June.

How Alexander learned of the crossing: before the Zakret ball from a Kovno dispatch reported by de Sanglen (Kudrinsky) vs told by Balashov during the ball (the usual version, repeated on ru.wikipedia without a source). Either way the date is 24 June (12 June OS).
HQ on 16 Sep: Kulakovo (ru.wikipedia, on the right bank near the Borovsky ferry) vs 'the Bronnitsy area' (chronicle).

Arrival at Tarutino: HQ 2 Oct (20 Sep OS), army 3 Oct (21 Sep OS) per ru.wikipedia and the chronicle; ESBE dates the Tarutino stay from 22 Sep OS (4 Oct). Date the army left Krasnaya Pakhra: 26 Sep (14 Sep OS, to Babenki, ru.wikipedia) vs a move to the Voronovo area by 28 Sep (chronicle).

Tarutino strength on arrival is not firmly sourced: 85,000 incl. militia or 60,000 (Isaev), rising to 120-130,000 by departure; ESBE's 97,000 excludes Cossacks and militia. Reinforcement totals (recruits, the '26 Don Cossack regiments') were confirmed only from search-result summaries, not from a document.

Vilna strength: 27,464 (Kudrinsky) vs 42,000 with 200 guns (ESBE) vs 40,000 'effectives at the Neman' (en.wikipedia lead) vs 'no more than 12,000' (RBS) vs 70,000 (Bogdanovich via en.wikipedia, evidently a wider definition). 27,464 = men in the ranks and 42,000 = with non-combatants is the usual reconciliation but I did not find a source stating that. The often-quoted '48,000 in hospital, 12,000 killed' breakdown was not confirmed online.
Strength at Drissa (mid-July) and the army's strength on leaving Moscow (14 Sep): no sourced figure found. Shvedov's 64,000 regulars after Borodino could not be verified at source (PDF unavailable).

HQ 20-22 Nov: Lanniki/'Laninka' (chronicle) vs Romanovo (heading of a Kutuzov letter of 8 Nov OS = 20 Nov; Sinelnikov also mentions Romanovo and 'Danniki'). Probably successive nights; order not established.
HQ 31 Oct and 4 Nov not found (31 Oct: marching north toward Vereya then west; Durnovo's diary has HQ at 'Spasskoye' before Silenki on 1 Nov. 4 Nov: presumably still Bykovo).

Kutuzov's words on hearing Napoleon had left Moscow ('...from this moment Russia is saved') come from Bolgovskoy's recollection as retold by Tolstoy and Rakovsky; I found no online text of Bolgovskoy's own memoir, so no verbatim quote is given. Night of 22/23 Oct (10/11 Oct OS) at Letashevka.
Maloyaroslavets: town changed hands 8 times (ru.wikipedia) vs 'about fifteen' (chronicle). Losses: about 7,000 a side (chronicle, ru.wikipedia) vs 3,000 in Kutuzov's report.

Coordinates left null (no unambiguous Wikipedia article): Priluki, Staroye Selo, Durykino, Krutitsy/Repishche, Adamovskoye, Silenki, Bykovo, Krasnoye, Gavryukovo, Bely Kholm (the Glinka-district village of that name lies WEST of Yelnya and is probably not the one), Baltutino, Shchelkanovo, Yurovo, Shilovo, Morozovo, Somry, Mikheevichi, Shevernichi, Usha, Beloruchi. 'Dobroye' = Bolshaya Dobraya and 'Kosino' = Kosino (Logoisk district) are probable identifications only.
